findings.claim: Every new attribute line is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so nothing generated for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework targets is decorated. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and it can be applied to classes on both. The derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist, and the requirement says ALL generated code is decorated. A common case is a library that targets only netstandard2.0 and is tested from a net8.0 test project: coverage is measured on the netstandard2.0 build, which still has none of the attributes. That is exactly the skew the requirement wants removed. The same guard appears in every template (Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Enum, Union, Resolver, CompositeResolver and their .cs counterparts).

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageNetStandardTests.GeneratedTypesExcludedWhenTargetingNetStandard20. It compiles against ReferenceAssemblies.NetStandard.NetStandard20 with the NETSTANDARD2_0 symbol defined. It first asserts that the attribute type resolves in that compilation, then asserts that every generated type carries the attribute. Expected to fail on head because the #if strips the attribute.

findings.claim: The README says the attribute is 'only emitted for targets where it is available (not netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework)'. That is factually wrong: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on both. The docs justify the coverage gap with a false premise.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare with the netstandard2.0 reference assembly (netstandard.dll contains System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute) and the .NET Framework 4.0+ System.dll. The same check is executed as the first assertion of ExcludeFromCodeCoverageNetStandardTests (GetTypeByMetadataName is non-null under NetStandard20 references).

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always on, no setting: every formatter and resolver template unconditionally emits [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. The change implements this, though it also guards the attribute with #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: On by default with an opt-out setting, which the requirement explicitly calls acceptable. Add a boolean option to GeneratorOptions/FormattersOptions (e.g. ExcludeFromCodeCoverage = true), readable from the existing generator options source (assembly attribute or analyzer config). Pass it to each template (Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Enum, Union, Resolver, CompositeResolver) and emit the attribute lines only when it is true. Add a test showing no attribute when the option is turned off.
